title: Ledger Library
tagline: Work the front desk of a grand library and learn how databases keep every record in its place.

funFacts.text: Every time you search a library catalogue, you are asking a database a question. Most of the world's apps keep their information the same way: in tables of rows and columns.
The relational model, the idea behind tables of rows and columns, was described by Edgar Codd in 1970.
SQLite, a tiny database engine that runs inside apps, is described by its makers as likely the most widely deployed software of its kind.
A database that joins a table of 6 members to a table of 9 loans with no matching rule would produce 54 rows of nonsense. The matching rule matters.

starRules: 3 stars: no mistakes and no hints. 2 stars: up to 2 mistakes. 1 star: you finished.
